subject: Marketplace bundling, outage SLAs and channel protection
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightlayerhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer question — bundling + outage credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Two procurement items came up we need clarified before internal legal signs off: 1) we want to publish a single bundled SKU in the GCP marketplace (core inference + extra tokens + managed alerts). How will list-price vs committed pricing map to the private offer? Specifically: can the bundle keep a single list price while the private offer gives a blended discount across the underlying SKUs?

2) we need clear outage/SLA credit mechanics for marketplace purchases. If BrightLayer is on a reseller path, we need to preserve channel margin in the event of credits — procurement wants an example waterfall showing how credits flow to reseller vs Redwood net rev.

Can you send a short proposal and sample mechanics? We want to move to signature next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
VP Procurement
BrightLayer Health

Attachment: procurement-rfi-questions.pdf (stub)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightlayerhealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer question — bundling + outage credits

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers up front, details and worked examples below and attached.

1) Bundled listing + private offer mapping: yes — you can publish a single marketplace SKU that appears at list price, while the private offer references the underlying entitlements. The private offer will apply an overall discount that we map against the sum of underlying SKU MSRP to produce customer net price. For accounting and channel margin purposes we provide an allocation report that maps the private-offer discount back to each internal SKU so the reseller gets the negotiated pass-through for their portion.

2) SLA credits and margin protection: we propose a two-part approach — (A) outage credit mechanics (standard marketplace credit issued to customer by Redwood), and (B) channel-protection addendum that preserves the reseller margin by applying credits pro rata to Redwood net revenue first, with a reserve waterfall that protects brokered margin for 90 days (or until true-up). This is operationalized in the channel-protect addendum.

Attached: Bundling-Proposal-v1.xlsx (worksheets: SKU-allocation, pricing-blend, sample-invoice), SLA-Credits-Matrix.pdf, Channel-Protect-Addendum-draft.docx

Next steps I suggest: Irene to confirm the exact reseller pass-through %, Ben to validate legal language for addendum, then we publish a private offer draft and a DocuSign for signature.

Ping me with any urgent questions.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123

Looping myself in on ops / billing details. A couple of practical constraints from Finance:

- We need the allocation mapping to be deterministic (no free-form percentages). The XLS has an allocation sheet where discounts are distributed by fixed SKU weights (we'll ask marketing/product for weights if needed).
- For SLA credits the recommended route is to issue credits to the customer account, then run a monthly true-up where the channel holdback is adjusted. That matches marketplace constraints (GCP/AWS flow-through).
- For reseller margin protection, legal wants the addendum to include a clause that credits impacting Redwoods net revenue are applied before any retroactive reductions to reseller commissions for the quarter — effectively protecting reseller margin during the true-up period.

Ben — can you weigh in on the margin % you expect the partner to require and whether a 90-day reserve is workable? I can draft a short paragraph for the addendum.

Irene Choi
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com

Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private offer question — bundling + outage credits

Irene — 90-day reserve is acceptable. For margin expectation: BrightLayer's GTM suggests they want a consistent 22% net margin on the resale. Two quick notes:

- If the private offer discount is material (>35%), we'll need to tier the reseller commission so the first $X of credits are absorbed by Redwood net rev protection and subsequent credits reduce reseller payouts. The attached Channel-Protect-Addendum-draft has a sample waterfall that implements this.
- Ops can run a monthly true-up and post an adjustment credit memo to the reseller if credits were applied to customers, but we should avoid retroactive negative invoices to customers.

Rishi — if you can confirm the SKU weights by Monday I will finalize the addendum language and we can push the DocuSign for signature. Samantha — happy to set a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through the waterfall.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
